## Keep going after the session

- **The Consultant's OS course**, the full semester-length version of Saturday's framework: [byu-strategy.github.io/management-consulting](https://byu-strategy.github.io/management-consulting/)
- **AI PM Bootcamp**, the full build curriculum behind Friday's workshop (vibe coding, spec-driven development, git + deployment, power users): [byu-strategy.github.io/ai-pm-bootcamp](https://byu-strategy.github.io/ai-pm-bootcamp/)
- **OpenAlex**, the open catalog of the world's research that powers both the data room and Research Scout: [openalex.org](https://openalex.org)

## Foundational readings: rigor, relevance, impact, and publishing incentives

The reading list behind the consulting case's data room. ★ = full grounding document in the data room.

### The outside-discipline anchors (economics)

- ★ Akerlof, G. A. (2020). Sins of Omission and the Practice of Economics. *Journal of Economic Literature*. [doi:10.1257/jel.20191573](https://doi.org/10.1257/jel.20191573), hardness over-rewarded vs. importance; the case's both/and grounding text.
- ★ Heckman, J. J., & Moktan, S. (2020). Publishing and Promotion in Economics: The Tyranny of the Top Five. *Journal of Economic Literature*. [doi:10.1257/jel.20191574](https://doi.org/10.1257/jel.20191574), top-journal publication as tenure currency.

### The field's own reckoning

- ★ Hambrick, D. C. (1994). What if the Academy Actually Mattered? *Academy of Management Review*. [doi:10.2307/258833](https://doi.org/10.2307/258833), the founding text of the debate.
- ★ Ghoshal, S. (2005). Bad Management Theories Are Destroying Good Management Practices. *Academy of Management Learning & Education*. [doi:10.5465/amle.2005.16132558](https://doi.org/10.5465/amle.2005.16132558)
- Pfeffer, J., & Fong, C. T. (2002). The End of Business Schools? Less Success Than Meets the Eye. *AMLE*. [doi:10.5465/amle.2002.7373679](https://doi.org/10.5465/amle.2002.7373679)
- Bennis, W. G., & O'Toole, J. (2005). How Business Schools Lost Their Way. *Harvard Business Review*. (No DOI, HBR.)
- Tourish, D. (2020). The Triumph of Nonsense in Management Studies. *AMLE*. [doi:10.5465/amle.2019.0255](https://doi.org/10.5465/amle.2019.0255)

### The rigor–relevance debate proper

- ★ Rynes, S. L., Bartunek, J. M., & Daft, R. L. (2001). Across the Great Divide: Knowledge Creation and Transfer Between Practitioners and Academics. *Academy of Management Journal*. [doi:10.2307/3069460](https://doi.org/10.2307/3069460)
- Rynes, S. L., Colbert, A. E., & Brown, K. G. (2002). HR Professionals' Beliefs About Effective Human Resource Practices. *Human Resource Management*. [doi:10.1002/hrm.10029](https://doi.org/10.1002/hrm.10029)
- Van de Ven, A. H., & Johnson, P. E. (2006). Knowledge for Theory and Practice. *Academy of Management Review*. [doi:10.5465/amr.2006.22527385](https://doi.org/10.5465/amr.2006.22527385)
- Rousseau, D. M. (2006). Is There Such a Thing as "Evidence-Based Management"? *Academy of Management Review*. [doi:10.5465/amr.2006.20208679](https://doi.org/10.5465/amr.2006.20208679)
- Kieser, A., & Leiner, L. (2009). Why the Rigour–Relevance Gap in Management Research Is Unbridgeable. *Journal of Management Studies*. [doi:10.1111/j.1467-6486.2009.00831.x](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-6486.2009.00831.x), paired with Hodgkinson, G. P., & Rousseau, D. M. (2009). …It's Already Happening! *JMS*. [doi:10.1111/j.1467-6486.2009.00832.x](https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-6486.2009.00832.x)

### Incentives, metrics, and market structure

- ★ Larivière, V., Haustein, S., & Mongeon, P. (2015). The Oligopoly of Academic Publishers in the Digital Era. *PLOS ONE*. [doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0127502](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0127502) (open access)
- Edwards, M. A., & Roy, S. (2017). Academic Research in the 21st Century: Maintaining Scientific Integrity in a Climate of Perverse Incentives and Hypercompetition. *Environmental Engineering Science*. [doi:10.1089/ees.2016.0223](https://doi.org/10.1089/ees.2016.0223) (open access)
- Bergstrom, T. C. (2001). Free Labor for Costly Journals? *Journal of Economic Perspectives*. [doi:10.1257/jep.15.4.183](https://doi.org/10.1257/jep.15.4.183)
- Alvesson, M., & Sandberg, J. (2011). Ways of Constructing Research Questions: Gap-Spotting or Problematization? *Organization*. [doi:10.1177/1350508410372151](https://doi.org/10.1177/1350508410372151)

### The constructive program

- George, G., Howard-Grenville, J., Joshi, A., & Tihanyi, L. (2016). Understanding and Tackling Societal Grand Challenges through Management Research. *Academy of Management Journal*. [doi:10.5465/amj.2016.4007](https://doi.org/10.5465/amj.2016.4007)
- Wickert, C., Post, C., Doh, J. P., Prescott, J. E., & Prencipe, A. (2020). Management Research that Makes a Difference: Broadening the Meaning of Impact. *Journal of Management Studies*. [doi:10.1111/joms.12666](https://doi.org/10.1111/joms.12666)
- Aguinis, H., Shapiro, D. L., Antonacopoulou, E. P., & Cummings, T. G. (2014). Scholarly Impact: A Pluralist Conceptualization. *AMLE*. [doi:10.5465/amle.2014.0121](https://doi.org/10.5465/amle.2014.0121)
- RRBM (2017). A Vision of Responsible Research in Business and Management. Position paper. [rrbm.network](https://www.rrbm.network/) (white paper, no DOI)
